description:
The contention hot path: atomic claims for every inventory model, cart holds with TTL, operational holds (house/artist/kills), channel allocations with caps/release rules, group/agency long-lived reservations, best-available seat selection.

**Conditions of Success:**
- No oversell under adversarial concurrent load (sustained load test in the gate)
- Staff can place/release/convert named operational holds
- Inventory splits across channels with per-channel caps and scheduled releases
- Best-available returns contiguous seats honoring map adjacency

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

**Amended (grilling):** Design-target on-sale (owner NFR): ~50-100k capacity event, 100k+ concurrent buyers in the waiting room, thousands of checkout attempts/min sustained. Load-test COS use these numbers. Per ADR-005, this core claims slots for every vertical (shows, festivals, parks, lodging, passes).

---
**Decomposed 2026-07-16** → US-012…US-019 (TKT-75…TKT-82); story text of record: docs/product/prd-v1.md §TKT-4. Occupancy capping out per ADR-013; festival pass products TKT-14; agency payment terms TKT-34; channel registry TKT-17.

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.
Backlog grilling 2026-07-12 (owner decisions): festival-scale NFR quantified; ADR-005 single claim core confirmed.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Sizing | ✅ | 8 vertical slices, each one reviewable PR; each demoable via API + availability read (staff UI is TKT-22's scope) |
| Dependencies | ⚠️ | US-017→TKT-3 (epic, not started) and US-018→US-017 wired as hard blockers; US-015/US-016→US-014 soft (same claim-model surface — parallelizable if Planning confirms no schema overlap) |
| AC verifiability | ✅ | Every AC test- or measurement-backed; no "works correctly" |
| Prefactoring | ✅ | None needed — ADR-010 explicitly designed the extension path ("seats, date ranges, entitlements reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering") |
| Cycle check | ✅ | TKT-3→TKT-80→TKT-81 is the only chain; acyclic |
| Context-mémo | ✅ | Baked on all 8 children (governingAdrs incl. ADR-010/005/013/017/022 per area) |
| Open decisions | ⚠️ | US-019 scope is `open, owner: human` |

**Concerns:**
1. **US-017/US-018 (TKT-80/81) are dead until TKT-3 ships.** The epic cannot close its best-available COS without the seat-map epic. Owner call: pull TKT-3 next, or accept TKT-4 closing partially with the seated stories re-parented.
2. **US-019 gate-profile split needs the owner** — the COS says "sustained load test in the gate"; the proposal is a scaled sustained profile in `make check` + the full NFR profile on demand. Marked `open, owner: human` on the child.
3. **Soft ordering US-014 → US-015/US-016**: not wired as blockers to keep them claimable, but all three touch the claim-type surface; claiming them concurrently risks migration conflicts. Recommendation: land US-014 first.
4. **Shared-festival-capacity claim mechanics** (PRD deferred-items list names TKT-4/TKT-14): schema-3 shared pools already claim through the core today, so nothing was cut here — pass *products* over shared capacity remain TKT-14.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — decomposition is sound and 6 of 8 children are claimable on prioritization; the owner decides concerns 1–2 at Gate 1.
